record.paper_title: Some Open Questions in Wave Chaos
record.context_brief: Exceptional eigenstates and genericity of QUE
record.original_question: Can Quantum Unique Ergodicity be disproved by constructing a negatively curved manifold and a sequence of exceptional high-energy eigenstates of the Laplacian, or of a lower-order perturbation of the Laplacian, whose semiclassical measures do not converge to Liouville measure? More generally, does QUE hold only for generic negatively curved surfaces or generic lower-order perturbations rather than for every negatively curved system?

evidence.quote: On the other hand, disproving QUE amounts to exhibiting a negatively curved manifold and a sequence of exceptional eigenstates of the Laplacian, or of some perturbation of it by lower-order terms.
Like the BGS conjecture, it is possible that QUE holds only for “generic” negatively curved surfaces, or “generic” perturbations of the Laplacian.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth compact Riemannian manifold of negative sectional curvature, and let $\Delta_g$ denote the (nonpositive) Laplace–Beltrami operator on $M$. Consider an orthonormal basis $\{\psi_n\}_{n\ge 1}\subset L^2(M)$ of eigenfunctions, $-\Delta_g\psi_n=\lambda_n\psi_n$, with $\lambda_n\to\infty$. To each $\psi_n$ one associates (via a choice of quantization) a semiclassical/microlocal lift, a probability measure $\mu_n$ on the unit cotangent bundle $S^*M$; any weak-$*$ limit of such a sequence is called a semiclassical (quantum) limit and is invariant under the geodesic flow. Let $\mu_L$ denote the normalized Liouville measure on $S^*M$.

The Quantum Unique Ergodicity (QUE) conjecture asserts that for every such $(M,g)$ the only semiclassical limit is $\mu_L$. More generally, the same statement is conjectured for the eigenfunctions of $-\Delta_g+V$, where $V$ is a lower-order (e.g. zeroth-order) perturbation.

Address the following:

(a) Construct, or prove the nonexistence of, a compact negatively curved Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$ (possibly together with a lower-order perturbation of $\Delta_g$) and a subsequence of eigenfunctions $\{\psi_{n_k}\}$ whose associated semiclassical measures converge weakly-$*$ to a probability measure $\mu\neq \mu_L$ on $S^*M$.

(b) Determine whether QUE holds for every compact negatively curved manifold (and every lower-order perturbation), or only for a generic such manifold/perturbation in a suitable Baire/measure-theoretic sense.
artifact.status_search_result: The Rudnick–Sarnak Quantum Unique Ergodicity conjecture for general compact negatively curved manifolds remains widely open. Significant partial progress includes Lindenstrauss's proof of arithmetic QUE on congruence surfaces, Anantharaman's entropy lower bounds, and Dyatlov–Jin full-support results on negatively curved surfaces. No counterexample has been constructed in the negatively curved setting, and the question of whether QUE holds universally or only generically remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Background on the Quantum Unique Ergodicity conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: The QUE conjecture for compact negatively curved manifolds remains open in general; arithmetic cases have been resolved.
status_evidence.claim: QUE on general negatively curved manifolds is open; only special (arithmetic) cases are settled.

status_evidence.title: Recent progress on the quantum unique ergodicity conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of progress on QUE, indicating the general conjecture is still open.
status_evidence.claim: The general QUE conjecture remains unresolved as of recent surveys.

status_evidence.title: Control of eigenfunctions on negatively curved manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work (Dyatlov–Jin and others) shows full support of semiclassical measures on negatively curved surfaces, but does not establish QUE.
status_evidence.claim: State-of-the-art results give full support but not equidistribution; QUE remains open.
